title: An open map with irreducible target and irreducible fibres over a dense set of points has irreducible source

standard_prerequisites.name: The definition of irreducibility through the impossibility of writing the space as a union of two proper closed subsets, and the openness of the map
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's section on irreducible components, immediately before the counted statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the three hypotheses (a), (b), (c) and the conclusion.

core_obligations: Assume a decomposition: the proof supposes that the source is the union of two closed subsets and passes to the two open sets obtained by removing one from the other, aiming to show one of them is empty (proof lines 1343-1345).

Push forward along the open map: by openness the images of the two open sets are open in the target, and irreducibility of the target forces one of them to miss a point of the dense set of hypothesis (c) (proof lines 1345-1349).
Use the irreducible fibre: at such a point the fibre is irreducible and the two open sets restrict to a separation of the fibre, which is impossible (proof lines 1349-1352).
Conclusion: one of the two closed subsets must be the whole source, so the source is irreducible (proof line 1352).
proof_roadmap: 反设 X = Z_1 ∪ Z_2（Z_i 闭），取 U_i = Z_i \ Z_j；由 f 开，f(U_i) 是 Y 中开集，Y 不可约迫使其中之一错过假设 (c) 的那个稠密集中的某点。
在该点处纤维不可约，而 U_1、U_2 在其上给出纤维的分离，矛盾；故 X 不可约。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is a topological criterion for irreducibility of the source of an open map (author lemma at source lines 1331-1340, label lemma-irreducible-on-top), under the hypotheses that the target is irreducible and that the fibres over a dense set of points are irreducible. The proof (source lines 1342-1353) uses all three hypotheses in a genuine way: openness pushes the two pieces of a presumed separation into the target, irreducibility of the target picks a point of the dense set where one piece misses, and irreducibility of the fibre there contradicts the existence of the separation (proof lines 1345-1352). The lemma is used in this chapter and in the Stacks treatment of morphisms to propagate irreducibility. H2.
